channel.title: Spotlight Delaware – Bias and Credibility - Article Feed
channel.description: Latest articles from Spotlight Delaware – Bias and Credibility (spotlightdelaware.org)

item.title: Dover moves to oust city manager, tensions revealed
item.description: Dover quietly put its city manager on paid administrative leave earlier this month -- the first step toward permanently removing him.

item.title: Delaware holds hearing on hotly contested primary care reform bill
item.description: Delaware senators held their first debate Wednesday over a health care reform proposal that would prioritize investments for primary care.

item.title: New data center regulations go into effect, but not for Delaware City proposal
item.description: New Castle County Executive Marcus Henry signed new data center regulations into law Wednesday, becoming the first in Delaware to do so.

item.title: Wilmington Senior Center abruptly shuts its doors, doesn't say why
item.description: Days after posting their March lunch menu onto social media, officials from the Wilmington Senior Center closed the doors of the 70-year-old facility.

item.title: State will close Georgetown charter school at end of academic year
item.description: Delaware education officials announced Thursday that the state will move forward with closing a Georgetown charter school due to persistent struggles with low enrollment.

item.title: Get Involved: Data center appeal, opioid settlement funds, budgets unveiled, more
item.description: A rundown of some of the most important or interesting public meetings happening around Delaware this week.

item.title: Democrats want to boost solar power through two bills in the General Assembly
item.description: Delaware lawmakers advanced two bills last week that would remove regulatory obstacles facing solar projects, just as the state scrambles to increase energy production amid soaring electricity prices.

item.title: Carney calls for a $20M housing fund in next Wilmington budget
item.description: Wilmington Mayor John Carney introduced his city budget Thursday and within it was a proposal to create a $20 million program to incentivize the construction of new housing.

item.title: Delaware approves $475K in opioid grants for local governments
item.description: The Delaware Prescription Opioid Settlement Distribution Commission approved three grants on Monday for Seaford, Wilmington and Newark.

item.title: Delaware proposes regulations on crypto, with licensing for stablecoins
item.description: With two bills introduced Monday, Delaware could become one of the first states to regulate the use of stablecoins in finance.
